title: Ambiguous relational reference and directed comparison
subtitle: Paper example (Fig. 1c) · 6 construction steps
provenance: Construction steps documented in the paper (Fig. 1c, Sections 1 and 3.1–3.5, Appendix C)

images.alt: Film still showing two women, labeled candidate A on the left and candidate B in profile on the right
images.caption: Input image (one scene, two depicted candidates A and B)

question: For the woman in the image whose first Golden Globe nomination was for a supporting role, what is her first nomination year minus the other woman's? Use award ceremony years.
answer: Year difference u − v (requires both candidates' first Golden Globe nomination years)

construction.ce: Directed comparison u − v: both u (Candidate A) and v (Candidate B) are required.

turns.label: GR
turns.summary: Establish grounded candidates in the source image

observation.text: Source annotations or visual analysis and retrieval establish grounded identities and provenance for candidates A and B. The visible cue "the woman in the image" fits both women (|C(V, ν)| > 1), so a retrieved condition must select one.

turns.label: RA
turns.summary: Search every candidate to resolve the relational reference
turns.input:
reference ρ = (ν = "the woman in the image", φ = "first Golden Globe nomination was for a supporting role")
requirement: M(V, ρ; F) = {e*} (one supported match; all alternatives ruled out)

observation.text: For ambiguous relational references, construction searches every candidate in C(V, ν), supports one match, and rules out all alternatives (unresolved cases are rejected). In Figure 1(c), Candidate A matches (Supporting role) and Candidate B is ruled out (Leading role), deciding whose year is u.

turns.label: SR
turns.summary: Retrieve target-specific evidence and record provenance
turns.input:
targets: {A (matched referent), B (the other woman)}
fact: first Golden Globe nomination year (award ceremony years)

observation.text: Construction searches each selected target and records its retrieved facts, sources, and image provenance. In Figure 1(c), this assigns Year u to Candidate A and Year v to Candidate B.

turns.label: CE
turns.summary: Compose both years into a directed comparison u − v
turns.input:
contributions: z_1 = Year u (A), z_2 = Year v (B)
relation: c(u, v) = u − v
requirements: Y_c([k]) = {a} and |Y_c([k] \ {j})| > 1 for every j

observation.text: Compositional Evidence requires joint sufficiency and individual necessity: all designated facts determine one answer, and removing any one leaves it undetermined. In Figure 1(c), both u and v are needed to determine the directed comparison u − v.

turns.label: PR
turns.summary: Check the question alone for text-only identity or answer leakage
turns.input:
question_only_probe(q)  # input image withheld
retention criterion: g_ref(T) = g_sup(T) = g_dep(T) = 1 and b(T) = 0

observation.text: The relational condition must remain non-unique outside the image. A bounded question-only search probe tests whether web search from the question alone recovers an identity or the answer; a task is kept only when g_ref = g_sup = g_dep = 1 and b(T) = 0, and flagged tasks are revised or discarded.

turns.label: TR
turns.summary: Collect verified teacher trajectories for supervised fine-tuning
turns.input:
teacher: Qwen3.7-Plus + search tools
inputs: (img_1, q)  # reference answer and synthesis records withheld

observation.text: The teacher (Qwen3.7-Plus) receives only the image and question and solves retained tasks with search tools. Protocol-valid trajectories whose final answers are judged correct against the reference answer are retained for one SFT stage on Qwen3.5-27B.

takeaway: What changes? RA ties the reference to the depicted candidates, and CE's directed comparison u − v needs both candidates' facts.
